plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, from pompons to spiders. It thrives in the shortening days of fall and is a staple of gardens and florists across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn (September to November in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan)
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants that set buds when nights lengthen. In Japan the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family, and the Chrysanthemum Throne is named after it.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A large, graceful tree that is covered in clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fern-like leaves fully emerge. Streets lined with jacarandas turn purple and carpet the ground with fallen blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in South Africa (Pretoria), Australia (Brisbane, Sydney) and Argentina
plants.funFact: In Pretoria, known as the Jacaranda City, there are tens of thousands of jacaranda trees, and local lore holds that a blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: A bulb that sends up goblet-shaped pink-lilac flowers in autumn with no leaves present. The strap-like foliage appears only in the following spring, which gives the plant its nickname 'naked ladies'.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid autumn (September to October)
plants.location: Meadows and woodland edges in Europe, from the British Isles to the Balkans; also grown in gardens elsewhere
plants.funFact: The plant contains colchicine, a toxic alkaloid used in medicine to treat gout and by plant breeders to double chromosome numbers. It is not related to true saffron crocus, despite the name.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall native North American wildflower that produces masses of daisy-like flowers with golden centers. It is a vital late-season nectar source for pollinators and thrives in prairies, meadows and roadsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Canada to the southern United States
plants.funFact: Monarch butterflies rely on New England asters for nectar to fuel their long southward migration, which often passes through just as the flowers peak in mid October.
